claims.claim: The PRD locks the Reverse deletion strategy to the invariant that rollingSync.steps stays a strictly sequential, one-match-group-at-a-time list 'for as long as this feature exists,' but T-28755 proposes parallel step groups inside that same rollingSync.steps structure. Adopting parallel steps silently breaks the last-in-first-out ordering Reverse depends on; unwinding requires either excluding parallel groups from Reverse entirely or a coordinated redesign of the deletion strategy, needing agreement from both the deletion-strategy owners and whoever implements T-28755.

T-28927's maturity-review scope call freezes strategy.rollingSync.steps' matchExpressions-list shape as the backward-compatible v1 contract once Progressive Sync ships Stable. T-28755's parallel-steps proposal changes exactly that shape, so if Stable ships first, parallel steps can only land as a new coexisting field rather than an in-place restructuring. That locks in two permanent step-expression mechanisms; collapsing them back to one later requires a deprecation cycle across every existing rollingSync.steps consumer, gated by the same back-compat bar that froze the shape.

rfc-002's CommitManifests proto2 message marks repoURL, targetBranch, drySHA, commitAuthor, commitMessage, and commitTime as required, a wire commitment that can never be relaxed once shipped clients depend on it. T-27327's proposed rollback flow (checkout an old rendered tree and re-push) is exactly the second caller the RFC didn't design for: it isn't hydrating a fresh dry commit, yet must still populate all six required fields with values that don't map cleanly onto what it's doing. Undoing this coupling later needs a new message/RPC version, since the existing required fields can't be loosened for callers already built against them.

rfc-001 moves the application-sync privilege boundary onto the destinationServiceAccounts-impersonated SA but never extends that boundary to the diff codepath, which still runs under the raw cluster Secret identity. T-28695 shows this gap forces external-cluster operators to keep broadening a single cluster-role's patch grant (five rounds and counting) as the only workaround, re-coupling exactly the control-plane/application-privilege split rfc-001 set out to decouple. Reversing it requires shipping diff-path impersonation and then a separate migration to walk back every already-granted resource kind on the standing credential.

rfc-001 explicitly decides impersonation SA selection is determined 'on a per Application level rather than on a per resource level,' meaning one resolved SA covers every resource in a sync. T-27833 needs exactly the per-resource split the RFC rejected (control-plane SA for Namespace creation, impersonated SA for everything else in the same Application). Retrofitting that requires revisiting a granularity decision the RFC's approvers already closed, not an additive change, since destinationServiceAccounts matching assumes one SA per Application sync.

rfc-002 recommends git push secrets be stored in a namespace separate from the rest of the Argo CD components for extra protection, but T-28239 places the hydrated-commit signing key Secret in the same namespace as the rest of the control plane, so any component already permitted to read Secrets there can read the key and produce commits that pass SourceIntegrity verification on the hydrated branch. Combined with the ticket's fail-fast startup behavior, a bad key crash-loops commit-server for the whole fleet, moving to an isolated namespace or to per-project keys later ('out of scope for now') is a migration requiring coordination between whoever owns RBAC in the control-plane namespace and every hydrator-enabled team depending on the single cluster-wide key.
